rules.title: SF Rent Ordinance § 37.10C: ban on algorithmic rent-setting devices
rules.requirement: Landlords and others may not sell or use algorithmic devices (software that analyzes nonpublic competitor rental data to recommend rents for vacant units) to set rents or manage occupancy levels for residential units. A tenant or the City Attorney can bring a civil action for violations.
rules.quoted_span: The law prohibits the sale or use of such algorithmic devices and allows a tenant or the City Attorney to bring a civil action if they believe an entity is in violation of the law.
rules.effective_date_note: Page states the legislation went into effect on October 14, 2024.
rules.key_value: ban on algorithmic devices using nonpublic competitor rental data
rules.penalty: Civil action by a tenant or the City Attorney

parsed.doc_summary: SF Rent Board news item (Oct 16, 2024) announcing Rent Ordinance § 37.10C, effective Oct 14, 2024, which bans the sale or use of algorithmic devices to set rents or manage occupancy and allows civil actions by tenants or the City Attorney.
